title: Strings That Repeat
statement: A binary string is a sequence $a_1a_2\dots a_{30}$ in which each $a_i$ is $0$ or $1$. For a positive integer $d < 30$, the string is said to have repeat length $d$ if $a_{i+d} = a_i$ for every integer $i$ with $1 \le i \le 30 - d$. How many binary strings of length $30$ have at least one of the repeat lengths $6$ and $10$, but do not have repeat length $15$?
hints: Start with a single repeat length $d$: which entries of the string can be chosen freely, and which are then forced? Next, suppose a string has repeat lengths $6$ and $10$, and compare $a_i$ with $a_{i+4}$ by going through a suitable third entry.

Write $R_d$ for the set of strings with repeat length $d$. Use inclusion-exclusion: $|A \cup B| = |A| + |B| - |A \cap B|$. Apply it once to $R_6 \cup R_{10}$, then again to the part of that union lying in $R_{15}$, which is the part to remove. The overlaps can be found by a subtractive Euclidean algorithm on repeat lengths.

If a string has repeat lengths $d < e$ with $d + e \le 30$, it also has repeat length $e - d$. This is checked by stepping through $a_{i+e}$ when that entry exists and through $a_{i-d}$ otherwise. Repeating this step gives $R_6 \cap R_{10} = R_2$, $R_6 \cap R_{15} = R_3$, $R_{10} \cap R_{15} = R_5$ and $R_3 \cap R_5 = R_1$. Since $|R_d| = 2^d$, now compute $|R_6 \cup R_{10}|$ and $|R_3 \cup R_5|$ and subtract.
solution:
Let $R_d$ be the set of strings with repeat length $d$. Then $|R_d|=2^d$, since $a_1,\dots,a_d$ are free and determine the rest. If a string has period $d$ and $d\mid e$, then it has period $e$, so $R_d\subseteq R_e$.

If a string has repeat lengths $d<e$ with $d+e\le 30$, then it has repeat length $e-d$. Indeed, for $i\le 30-(e-d)$: if $i+e\le30$, then $a_{i+e-d}=a_{i+e}=a_i$. Otherwise $i>30-e\ge d$, so $a_{i+e-d}=a_{i-d}=a_i$, using $e$ then $d$.

Hence $R_6\cap R_{10}$ gives repeat length $4$, then $2$, so $R_6\cap R_{10}=R_2$. Similarly $R_6\cap R_{15}$ gives $9$, then $3$, so it equals $R_3$ (as $R_3\subseteq R_6,R_{15}$). Also $R_{10}\cap R_{15}$ gives $5$, so it equals $R_5$. Finally $R_3\cap R_5$ gives $2$, then $1$, so it equals $R_1$. All sums used are at most $30$.

Then
$$|R_6\cup R_{10}|=2^6+2^{10}-2^2=1084.$$
The strings to remove are
$$(R_6\cup R_{10})\cap R_{15}=R_3\cup R_5,$$
of size $2^3+2^5-2^1=38$.

The count is $1084-38=1046$.
